source: arXiv:1610.00278v1, Appendix B, Lemma B.1(i)-(iv): compactness and bounded-set topology consequences
scope: Compact-set inverse weak-star continuity; additional consequences of already completed source clauses
results: An ambient map into original physical weak-star potentials with endpoint norm-bounded image is continuous iff EVERY original Fourier coefficient of the map is continuous.

Every continuous injective map from a weak-star CLOSED endpoint norm-BOUNDED physical subset into any original physical weak-star space is a CLOSED EMBEDDING. Its inverse on its exact image is continuous. Once forward continuity is known, no separate image bound is required for this conclusion.

For an injective map with endpoint norm-bounded image, continuity of all original Fourier coefficients gives a closed embedding on a closed bounded physical domain. The homeomorphism onto the EXACT physical image is explicitly constructed, with forward and inverse evaluation identities.

For every such continuous injective map, a domain constraint is closed iff its image is AMBIENT weak-star closed. Arbitrary-filter convergence of images to the image of a domain point is equivalent to convergence to that same original point.

When the image is also endpoint norm bounded, inverse convergence can independently use ANY admissible original lower finite-p norms on the two sides. The exact strict thresholds and both endpoint bounds are retained. In the article range this uses the IDENTICAL original H-minus-one distributions on both sides.
qualifications: All original Lemma B.1(i)-(iv) clauses were already proved; this milestone adds compact-set inverse-continuity consequences and does not claim an additional source clause.
The physical domain must be weak-star closed AND endpoint norm bounded. This does not assert inverse continuity on the entire unbounded physical space.
A bounded image is required for the coefficient continuity criterion and for the lower-norm image convergence criterion. It is not inferred from injectivity.
No actual KdV or Birkhoff map is constructed by these criteria. All five main theorems remain unproved.
Six unrelated uncommitted free Dirichlet/Fredholm/resolvent modules are preserved outside this milestone and excluded from its committed checker and exact declaration audit.
norm: Exact original FourierLebesgueSpace(2,-r,infinity) endpoint norm; full original real mean-zero physically period-one distributions retained.
parameters: All real domain and codomain orders. Independent finite Banach exponents p,q >=1 with (-s-t)*p.toReal>1 and (-r-u)*q.toReal>1. No nontrivial-filter assumption is needed for convergence equivalences.
